question: uniqueness
claim: Exact integer comparison returns all maximizing size-probability pairs, including the all-zero axes and the empty set. A positive-mean tie can only be adjacent, and a prime-power lower size cannot tie.
frontier: Existence of a positive-mean tie at a composite lower size with at least two prime factors is open.

question: uniqueness
claim: The unbounded full set is algebraically decidable for underdispersed data and after a strict witness over the active face or a strictly losing Poisson tail. Finite-size co-winners use exact algebraic height comparison.
frontier: A fitted NB face can require an unresolved arithmetic equality test. The vanishing fourth-order Poisson case and existence of nonconstant cross-size ties remain open.

question: uniqueness
claim: For a positive integer alpha, semialgebraic size-profile decomposition returns the full unbounded set including face equality. At NB equidispersion a nonzero quadratic coefficient resolves the tail direction for general holds.
frontier: A noninteger zero quadratic coefficient and the existence of nonconstant globally tied sizes remain open.

question: uniqueness
claim: At any known size the complete maximizing set is semialgebraic and decidable by real quantifier elimination. The attained identifiable branch has finitely many algebraic candidates and is unique through size eight.
frontier: Universal singleton status above size eight remains open.

question: uniqueness
claim: For positive means the Poisson supporting inequality is decidable by an exact critical-value test and rules out every finite winner when it holds, including two adjacent occupied counts. A compact certified canonical winner transports to one or two labels according to the seam.
frontier: Universal canonical cardinality and exact equality of general critical heights remain open.

question: uniqueness
claim: Binary data with a positive count have exactly one maximizer on the size-beta seam for every positive held alpha. The exact histogram (0,200) at alpha 2 instead has an attained off-seam swap pair.
frontier: The number of winning canonical orbits for general histograms and exact comparison of their heights remain open.

question: uniqueness
claim: The supported size scan has one candidate per identifiable attained size. An exact full-support saturation test yields a unique maximum for all saturated histograms detectable at sizes two and three or with rational dispersion at any size.
frontier: Exact general free-dispersion height comparison and uncapped CMP-face equality remain open.

question: uniqueness

frontier: General irrational holds and existence of a nonconstant rational-hold tie or a nonadjacent tie remain open.

question: uniqueness
claim: Attained fits have a finite analytic candidate set. Two-cell histograms on zero and K with a fixed positive fraction at each count are unique for sufficiently large K, uniformly for zero fractions from one quarter to three quarters when K is at least 2^28.
frontier: General score-root degeneracy and exact critical-height equality remain open.

question: uniqueness

question: uniqueness
claim: The Poisson maximizer is unique for one-sided adjacent-count histograms and more generally whenever the exact Poisson supporting-polynomial test passes. Other histograms have a finite analytic candidate set.
